name: Charalambides
label: Kranky
lede: Two clerks at a Houston record store named their band after a customer. They married, divorced and kept going, and when Tom Carter went into a coma in Berlin, other musicians made an album to pay his bills.

eras.title: The name belongs to a customer
eras.text: Two clerks at Houston's Sound Exchange, Tom Carter and Christina Carter, started playing with a roommate in late 1991. The name they ended up with belonged to a customer.

years.src: The Self-Portrait Gospel · COTFG: Christina Carter interview · Wikipedia
years.h: Mutual Admiration Society starts playing in Houston
years.p: Tom Carter's college roommate Kyle Silfer joins him and Christina Carter in late 1991, under the name Mutual Admiration Society.
years.xp:
Tom Carter grew up in Maryland and Ohio and came to Houston on a scholarship to the University of Houston, where he took an English degree. From 1989 to 1993 he also played in the Houston band The Mike Gunn. He and Christina worked together at Sound Exchange over those same years and "became friends that way."

Carter remembers Silfer playing guitar overhand, picking with his thumb. Christina Carter dates the real start of Charalambides to 1991.

years.h: The band is named after a record store customer
years.p: Charalambides is the surname of a customer at Sound Exchange, the Houston record shop where Tom and Christina Carter worked.

eras.title: Siltbreeze says yes to everything
eras.text: Tom Lax's Philadelphia label Siltbreeze, home of Harry Pussy and other outsider noise, gave Charalambides vinyl and room to sprawl. Christina Carter says Siltbreeze let them think in double albums from the start, without interference.

years.h: A C-100 cassette, and the band is a duo
years.p: Silfer is gone, so Tom and Christina Carter put out a 100-minute tape themselves. Kranky reissues Our Bed Is Green as a double CD in 2005.
years.xp: A second self-released tape, Historic 6th Ward, followed in 1994. The band's own Wholly Other label put it on CD in 1996, and Time-Lag pressed it as a double LP in 2002.

years.h: Tom Lax books them for the Khyber, and Jason Bill fills out the sound
years.p: Siltbreeze founder Tom Lax invites Charalambides to his 1993 festival at the Khyber in Philadelphia. Tom and Christina Carter bring in guitarist Jason Bill.
years.xp: Carter says Lax's lineup included Guided by Voices and Bassholes. He recruited Bill because, as he put it, Bill "told us he'd been playing for 10 years but still couldn't play 'real' songs."

years.src: Wikipedia: Siltbreeze · The Other Side of Life
years.h: Siltbreeze gives them their first vinyl
years.p: Union is the first Charalambides LP, on Tom Lax's Siltbreeze, the label he founded in 1989 out of his own fanzine.

years.h: Market Square makes it a double
years.p: The second Siltbreeze record is the first double album. The same year Playtime issues a 7-inch, Devils backed with Bid You Goodnight.
years.xp: Christina Carter says Siltbreeze made it "extremely easy" to think straight away in terms of "maximum effect, double albums."

years.h: Bad shows end the trio, and Jason Bill moves to El Paso
years.p: Tom Carter says the three-piece ended around 1996 after a run of bad shows. Bill left for El Paso and the Carters went back to being a duo.
years.xp: The trio years included touring with Siltbreeze labelmates Harry Pussy. By then the band had its own label, Wholly Other, releasing records since 1995.

eras.title: A label of their own, and a pedal steel player
eras.text: Charalambides ran its own label now, much of it hand-numbered CD-Rs in editions of 100 to 250. Pedal steel and a third voice came in, and the band landed in the circle of Six Organs of Admittance later filed as New Weird America.

years.h: Houston is the last album on Siltbreeze
years.p: Named for the band's hometown, it comes before the move to Kranky.

years.src: The Self-Portrait Gospel · Tiny Mix Tapes · Noisey
years.h: Heather Leigh Murray brings a pedal steel and a third voice
years.p: West Virginia-born, Houston-raised Murray becomes the third member around 2000. She stays through Joy Shapes.
years.xp: Murray also formed Scorces with Christina Carter, a duo of pedal steel and voices, and played in Houston's Taurpis Tula. She later worked with Jandek and Peter Brötzmann under the name Heather Leigh.

years.src: Tom Carter on Bandcamp: YIH · Wikipedia
years.h: A 100-copy duo record, and a split with Ben Chasny
years.p: Carbon Records issues the Austin-recorded duo improvisation YIH in 100 copies. Timelag pairs Charalambides with Ben Chasny's Six Organs of Admittance on a split LP.
years.xp: On YIH Tom Carter plays lap steel, bells and music box and Christina Carter plays chord organ and sings; the cover art is by Joe Tunis. The double LP IN CR EA SE followed on Eclipse in 2002.

eras.title: Kranky arrives as the marriage comes apart
eras.text: Kranky gave Charalambides real distribution for the first time. The best-known run of records came while the Carters' marriage came apart, Tom moved to California and Heather Leigh Murray moved to Scotland.

years.h: Unknown Spin, a CD-R split, becomes the first Kranky album
years.p: It is the band's half of a 2002 Wholly Other CD-R split with Scorces, Christina Carter's duo with Heather Leigh Murray.

years.src: The Other Side of Life · The Self-Portrait Gospel · Wikipedia
years.h: Joy Shapes gets made at home and edited on a computer
years.p: Tom Carter says all of Joy Shapes was recorded at home and edited from 4-track to DAT. Jerry Tubb mastered it at his Austin studio.
years.xp:
Carter described the record as "intensive and really heavy all the way through" and said it took a year. His line on the computer: "The main new instrument." He did editing and processing with it that he couldn't have done before.

It was Heather Leigh Murray's last record with the band. Extra material from the sessions came out as Electricity Ghost on Wholly Other in 2007.

years.src: The Self-Portrait Gospel · The Other Side of Life · Wikipedia
years.h: Tom and Christina Carter divorce, and Charalambides carries on
years.p: Tom Carter says his and Christina Carter's protracted breakup and divorce played out during the Joy Shapes sessions. In early 2004 he took a bookstore job in Berkeley.
years.xp:
Tom settled in Oakland while Christina stayed in Texas. Tom said in 2005 that living apart meant "big chunks of our lives will take place in the absence of the other."

Wikipedia still describes them as divorced but a musical unit.

years.big: "Heather fell in love and moved to Glasgow."
q: Heather fell in love and moved to Glasgow.
years.src: The Other Side of Life · Tiny Mix Tapes
years.h: Heather Leigh Murray moves to Glasgow
years.p: Christina Carter's explanation, in a 2005 interview. Murray co-runs the Volcanic Tongue shop and label there with writer David Keenan, and Charalambides is a duo again.
years.xp: Murray co-runs Volcanic Tongue with David Keenan; the shop and label are in Glasgow. Christina's full line to The Other Side of Life: "so for practical reasons Tom and I have to carry on as a duo."

years.cap: Charalambides live at Point Ephémère, Paris
yt: Live at KC Belgie, Hasselt, 2005, plus interview
years.h: Andrew MacGregor joins the Carters for A Vintage Burden
years.p: The third Kranky album of new music, made while Tom Carter lived in Oakland.

years.cap: Charalambides at the Turf Club, St. Paul, Minnesota, November 10, 2007
years.h: Likeness is the fourth for Kranky, and a vault album follows
years.p: The same year Wholly Other releases Strangle the Wretched Heavens, recorded 1994 to 1996.

eras.title: Forty days in a Berlin ICU
eras.text: Exile was the last Charalambides album on Kranky. On the European tour that followed, Tom Carter nearly died, and fellow musicians went to work on his bills.

years.h: Exile is the last Kranky album
years.p: The fifth Kranky album of new music. The Houston Chronicle later noted Christina Carter's lyrics and voice pushed further to the fore.

years.cap: Tom Carter playing live, May 19, 2012, twelve days before the hospital stay
q: Forty days in intensive care and three weeks in another facility
years.src: Houston Press · INDY Week · Houston Chronicle
years.h: Tom Carter checks into a Berlin hospital and goes into a coma
years.p: On a European tour, Carter checks in with pneumonia and goes into septic shock. Doctors put him in a medically induced coma.
years.xp:
Carter says he checked in hoping for antibiotics before the tour moved on to Glasgow, then blacked out. He spent about 40 days in intensive care, then moved in mid-July to a rehabilitation clinic in Ahrenshoop on the Baltic coast. The Houston Chronicle later reported it left him with a lasting heart-rhythm problem.

Treated out of network and overseas, he faced bills his insurance might not cover, and ex-wife and bandmate Christina Carter spoke for the band in the press.

years.h: Bill Orcutt and Pete Swanson put out a benefit album for Carter's bills
years.p: Music for Tom Carter also features [[Jefre Cantu-Ledesma|9b69c184-919f-4db2-a2a4-995024f69334]] and others, with all proceeds going to Tom Carter. Benefit shows ran from Houston and Chapel Hill to San Francisco and Portugal.
years.xp: Three Lobed Recordings gave Carter the proceeds from its unsold stock of his records, and donations went to a trust through helptomcarter.org. Exclaim reported he could not work or tour until the following year at the earliest.

eras.title: Home to Houston, under their own names
eras.text: After years apart in California, New York and elsewhere, both Carters were living in Houston again by 2018. Christina Carter says the album they cut in 2017 was the last time she recorded a note for years.

years.cap: Tom and Christina Carter at The Rose Hill, Brighton, November 24, 2018
years.src: The Vinyl District · The Reveille (KLSU) · Houston Chronicle · COTFG: Christina Carter interview
years.h: A double LP in three days, with no plan going in
years.p: Charalambides: Tom and Christina Carter comes out on Drawing Room, recorded with engineers Ryan Edwards and Shannon Smith. The Vinyl District counted more than 30 full-length releases by then.
years.xp:
Tom had moved back to Houston from New York around 2016, and Christina followed; the Houston Chronicle billed a show at Lawndale Art Center as their first Houston date in nearly a decade. The duo toured Europe that November.

Christina Carter has said she hasn't recorded a note since the 2017 sessions for this album.
